title: an-artifact-is-present-tense-or-past-tense-never-both
intention: Every artifact in the corpus is exactly one tense. PRESENT-TENSE (charters, CLAUDE.md, MAP.md, state files, code and its comments): rewritten at each design shift so it reads as written today, provenance shrunk to ticket-id pointers — git keeps every old version, so the rewrite loses nothing. PAST-TENSE (history, slates, voyages, decisions): append-only and permanent per Law 7, opened deliberately for archaeology, never loaded by default — EXCEPT through a compiled current-truth face (charter `state` compiled from `history`, the SessionStart slate injection). Corollaries: no periodic summarizing pass — the PROVED crossing's charter delta IS the summarizing event, rewriting to present tense while the voyage narrative freezes into history in the same act; migrations default to atomic-in-one-voyage, and a slow migration is legitimate only as a cast ticket whose cursor is the SOLE statement of how far along.
why: History creates noise: a model reader weights whatever is in context as if it were present tense, so an outdated bit of history reads as true (Akien's lived observation, 2026-08-15 — the idea's verbatim). The corpus's own house style feeds the leak by writing history INTO present-tense artifacts as dated-append paragraphs. This is Law 9 turned on the corpus's prose — an older paragraph is not evidence about the current design — and Law 1: a stale claim read as current makes the resolver re-litigate the settled.
traces_to: Law 9 (no past artifact outranks the source; an older translation is not evidence about it), Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel), Law 7 (deliberately KEPT: records of truth stay append-only — only their default-loadedness changes), Law 4 (the eventual shape-check enforcement, carried by child a-dated-append-in-a-charter-is-a-red)

falsifier.proves_green: concept-piece invariant: proved + feeds-back-on-failure. Prove gate: quorum signature — the quorum is Akien; his confirm on ruling 2026-08-15-an-artifact-is-present-tense-or-past-tense-never-both is the signature, recorded as a VALIDATION (method 'review by Akien', evidence his verbatim ruling). Kicks back on his rejection like a red build (CP2).
falsifier.proves_red: Done when: a shape-scan over the present-tense set finds zero dated-append paragraphs; the briefing surface structurally excludes history; a slow migration without a cast-ticket cursor is refusable. Wrong-intent tells: a rewrite loses design information git cannot recover; readers demonstrably need voyage narrative in default context; the per-voyage rewrite discipline costs more than the stale-history noise it removes.
falsifier.horizon: the watch clears after 10 consecutive charter writes land with zero new dated-append shapes
